chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever performs Umrah from Al-Tan'eem, let him not cut off the Talbiyya until he looks at the Masjid.

key_terms.المسجد: The Masjid (referring to the Sacred Mosque/Kaaba in this context)

ai.seo_question: When does the pilgrim stop reciting Talbiyya during Umrah from Tan'eem?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi specifies the Miqat of Al-Tan'eem as the starting point for Umrah pilgrims, mandating the continuous recitation of Talbiyya until the Sacred Mosque is in view. In Shia jurisprudence, this emphasizes the continuity of the state of Ihram and the spiritual focus required during the approach to the Kaaba, distinguishing it from Hajj protocols where Talbiyya may cease upon entering the Masjid al-Haram.
